Defines the JSON-LD schema templates (PDP, PLP, boutique, homepage — DMU-037 to DMU-040), the consolidated hreflang structure (DMU-025), and the CMS-editable on-page SEO field schema (DMU-035).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Specification documents per requirement ID; Accenture implements in SFCC / PWA. Final JSON-LD scope and page types to be confirmed before build (DMU-038).                                                                                                                                                |
| **Accessibility vendor** _(TBC by Zimmermann)_ | Manual accessibility audits, screen-reader and assistive-tech testing, audit cadence, remediation triage. Complements the automated coverage in §10.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Audit reports per cadence; defects raised back into the Accenture backlog. Vendor name, screen-reader / browser matrix, and cadence still pending from Zimmermann.                                                                                                                                        |
| **Tell No Lies**                               | Zimmermann's marketing technology partner. Owns the GTM container configuration and the downstream tags loaded inside GTM (GA4, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, etc.). The container is hosted on **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned managed tagging server) — Tell No Lies operates the Addingwell workspace, not just the GTM container. **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg** are loaded as PWA-direct head tags; Optimizely's script is supplied by Zimmermann. | Accenture's responsibility ends at emitting a comprehensive data layer (AAB-001 / AAB-002), embedding the GTM container ID + Addingwell tagging-server URL, and injecting the Optimizely/Crazy Egg head snippets (Didomi-gated). Tell No Lies consumes the data layer and configures the GTM-housed tags. |

---

## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type                                                         | Pattern                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages                | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server                                                                                                                                                                | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states                               | **SSR shell + CSR data**                                                                                                                                                                                             | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven                                                                                                                                        |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

---

## 9. Performance Strategy

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric                    | Target |
| ------------------------- | ------ |
| LCP (mobile p75)          | ≤ 2 s  |
| Lighthouse Performance    | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility  | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

---

## 10. Accessibility

**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, with WCAG 2.1 AA as the floor that is always met.

**Automated coverage:**

- axe-core via `vitest-axe` at the unit layer and `axe-playwright` at the E2E layer
- Storybook a11y addon at component level during development
- Lighthouse CI accessibility score ≥ 0.90 in the SIT gate

**Manual coverage:** delegated to Zimmermann's existing accessibility vendor (unconfirmed — vendor, screen-reader / browser matrix, and audit cadence to be supplied by Zimmermann).

---

## 11. Consent & Marketing

### 11.1 Didomi gating (REG-048–056)

- Cookie consent banner on first visit, all storefronts; preferences persist across sessions and are reviewable/updatable per category at any time.
- **No third-party tracking or marketing script loads until consent is granted** — including GTM (and the tags Tell No Lies loads downstream: Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, GA4, etc.), the PWA-direct head tags Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg (AAB-004/005), Inside Chat, Narvar widgets.
- **reCAPTCHA is not a tracking script** (CRM-008). It loads on register / login form interaction only, deferred to keep it off LCP. **Regional split:** in **EU & UK** it is consent-gated and loads only after Didomi consent — with the accepted consequence that a visitor who declines consent is never challenged, so reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection there. In **all other regions** it loads on form interaction regardless of consent state.
- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2**; hashed email passed at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions.
- Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed** — no third-party scripts load.
- Per-storefront consent defaults are specified under REG-054.

### 11.2 Marketing opt-in sync

`FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys` is the opt-in sync chain (REG-058, REG-059). Sync failures queue and retry silently — they never block the user flow. Trigger points (guest at order placement, registered at registration and My Account preference updates) are functional detail, out of scope for this TSD.

### 11.3 GDPR touchpoints in the PWA

GDPR fulfilment (DSAR, right-to-erasure, retention, breach reporting per REG-060–067) is handled by the SFCC GDPR cartridge and BM configuration — out of scope for this TSD. PWA-side touchpoints are limited to:

- Localised privacy policy pages, served from Contentful per storefront.
- The consent UI itself (covered in 11.1).
- Surfacing the customer-initiated erasure / data-export entry point in My Account where exposed by SFCC.

### 11.4 Didomi consent gate reference

Implementation reference for the PWA: which Didomi purpose / vendor ID gates each third-party script. All IDs are **TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.** Guesses are in brackets to orient the conversation.

> Didomi purpose IDs for the three declared categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051), plus per-environment Notice IDs, are open items (§12.1 / §12.2 of the Open Items register). All vendor-specific IDs below depend on those being provisioned first.

| Integration                                                          | Didomi purpose / vendor ID                                          | Scope                                  | Open item ref |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| **GTM (Addingwell)** — loads Meta, GA4, Pinterest, TikTok downstream | Handled by Tell No Lies in the GTM container / Addingwell workspace | All storefronts                        | —             |
| **Inside Chat**                                                      | TBC                                                                 | All storefronts                        | §14.1         |
| **Optimizely Web**                                                   | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | US storefront only                     | §15.2         |
| **Crazy Egg**                                                        | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | All storefronts                        | §16.3         |
| **Narvar Promise**                                                   | TBC (Analytics/Performance? from Narvar/Zimm?)                      | Domestic storefronts only              | §11.2         |
| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | n/a — no consent required; loads on form interaction                | All except EU & UK                     | —             |
| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | TBC                                                                 | EU & UK storefronts only               | §10.2         |
| **Measmerize**                                                       | TBC                                                                 | PDP only                               | §17.1         |
| **Vimeo**                                                            | TBC (Marketing/Analytics? use `dnt=1` if no consent)                | PDP + editorial pages, all storefronts | §18.1         |

---

## 12. Graceful Degradation

Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

| System                   | Failure mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

---------------------

Product data in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a **master catalogue** (`zimmermann-catalog`) with per-site **storefront catalogues** for navigation and category assignment. Product content (rich text, editorial imagery) is managed in **Contentful CMS**.

AP21 is the system of record for all product data. Product data flows from AP21 into SFCC via **MuleSoft** — there is no direct AP21 → SFCC integration. MuleSoft acts as the integration layer, transforming and routing product data into SFCC catalogue XML imports.

      "value": "1. Overview
-----------

Pricing in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a per-site, per-currency **pricebook** structure. Each site has a list price (RRP) and a sale price pricebook for each currency it supports. For Global-e sites (USIntl, EUIntl, ME, HK), SFCC holds prices in the base currency; Global-e handles currency conversion and localisation at checkout.

There is no direct MuleSoft price integration. Price feeds are expected to originate from **AP21** and are loaded into SFCC via data import (XML pricebooks).

---

2. Pricebook Architecture
-------------------------

### 2.1 Naming Convention

Defaultnone{site}-{currency}-list-prices ← RRP / list price
{site}-{currency}-sale-prices ← Sale price (parent = list pricebook)

**Examples:**`au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`, `usintl-usd-list-prices`, `euintl-eur-list-prices`

### 2.2 Pricebook Hierarchy

Sale pricebooks reference their parent list pricebook:

Defaultxml<header pricebook-id="au-aud-sale-prices">
<currency>AUD</currency>
<parent>au-aud-list-prices</parent>
</header>

SFCC resolves the effective price by checking the sale pricebook first, then falling back to list.

---

3. Pricebook Register — All Sites
---------------------------------

| --- | --- | --- |
| `au-aud-list-prices` | AUD | List |
| `au-aud-sale-prices` | AUD | Sale |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `uk-gbp-sale-prices` | GBP | Sale |

USD only. International orders from the US storefront are handled by ZimmermannUSIntl via Global-e.

| Pricebook | Currency | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `us-usd-list-prices` | USD | List |
| `us-usd-sale-prices` | USD | Sale |

### ZimmermannUSIntl (Global-e)

Base currency: **USD**. Global-e handles checkout currency conversion; MXN is a supported Global-e display currency for this site.

| `usintl-usd-sale-prices` | USD | Sale |
| `usintl-mxn-list-prices` | MXN | List |

460	### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment
461	
462	The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the _spread_ of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.
463	
464	#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)
465	
466	- **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
467	- **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.
468	
469	#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)
470	
471	`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
472	
473	> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.
474	
475	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
476	
477	| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                             | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
478	| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
479	| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                             | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
480	| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
481	| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                                | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
482	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                  | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
483	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                  | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |
484	| `google-places`        | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New)                                                                 | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059)                    | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly.                                                                                                                      |
485	| `booxi`                | Booxi base URL (TBD)                                                                                               | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167)                           | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
486	
487	**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).

491	## 13. Testing Strategy
492	
493	Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.
494	
495	| Layer                 | Tool             | Covers                                               |
496	| --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
497	| Unit                  | Vitest           | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
498	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions                   |
499	| E2E                   | Playwright       | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries  |
500	
501	### 13.1 What is tested
502	
503	Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.
504	
505	### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow
506	
507	Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.
508	
509	### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures
510	
511	E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)
512	
513	### 13.4 Selector priority
514	
515	Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.
516	
517	---
518	
519	## 14. CI/CD & Environments
520	
521	This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.
522	
523	### 14.1 Topology
524	
525	A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
526	
527	| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
528	| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
529	| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
530	| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
531	| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
532	| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
533	| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
534	| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |
535	
536	Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
537	
538	### 14.2 Branch model
539	
540	GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.
541	
542	| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       |
543	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
544	| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
545	| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
546	| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
547	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
548	| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
549	| `develop`, `main`         | —                      | protected; PR-only                                                              |
550	
551	Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.
552	
553	### 14.3 CI workflows
554	
555	**QA workflow (`qa.yml`)** — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:
556	
557	- Unit tests (Vitest)
558	- Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)
559	
560	**SIT gate (`digital-sit.yml`)** — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:
561	
562	- Playwright `p0` priority specs
563	- Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
564	- Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
565	- Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
566	- Trend gate against the LHCI history server
567	
568	### 14.4 Deployment
569	
570	Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:
571	
572	- **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
573	- **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
574	- **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
575	- **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
576	- **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions
577	
578	Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.
579	
580	MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`.

| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
| `develop`, `main`         | —                      | protected; PR-only                                                              |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (`qa.yml`)** — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

- Unit tests (Vitest)
- Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (`digital-sit.yml`)** — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

- Playwright `p0` priority specs
- Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
- Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
- Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
- Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

- **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
- **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
- **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
- **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
- **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`.

      "value": "1. Overview
-----------

Inventory in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by **NewStore** (OMS) and managed upstream by **AP21** (ERP). MuleSoft acts as the integration layer in both directions:

* **Inbound (AP21 → NewStore):** Stock levels are pushed from AP21 into NewStore on a scheduled basis (DC and store stock)
* **Outbound (NewStore → SFCC):** Inventory availability is exported from NewStore and imported into SFCC via a scheduled sync

SFCC does **not** connect to AP21 or NewStore directly — all inventory data passes through MuleSoft.

---

2. End-to-End Data Flow
-----------------------

DefaultnoneAP21 (ERP)
│
├──► stock-prc-api (DC stock) ──► NewStore ─────────────────────►┐
└──► stock-prc-api (Store stock) ──► NewStore │
│
NewStore ──► inventory-sync-prc-api ──► [export ZIP via S3] ──► SFCC│
│ │
(transform to SFCC format) │
▼ ▼
SFCC Inventory Import Job
(per-site inventory lists)

---

3. Inbound: AP21 → MuleSoft → NewStore
--------------------------------------

### 3.1 DC Stock Upload

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| API | `stock-prc-api` + `newstore-sys-api` |
| Trigger | Daily scheduler at 2:00 AM EST + on-demand REST endpoint |
| Scope | Distribution centre (DC) locations — delta + full |
| JIRA | ZMOBLD-263 |

**Flow:** 1. Scheduler triggers (or REST call with `fromDate` + `countryCode`) 2. MuleSoft validates DC IDs, stock quantities, and product info 3. Creates import job in NewStore (`POST /api/import`) 4. Starts the job (`POST /api/import/{id}/start`) 5. Polls job status (`GET /api/import/{id}`) until complete

### 3.2 Store Stock Upload

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| API | `stock-prc-api` + `newstore-sys-api` |
| Trigger | One-time full load (initial migration) + scheduler |
| Scope | All physical boutique locations |
| JIRA | ZMOBLD-248 |

**Flow:** 1. MuleSoft validates store IDs, quantities, and product info 2. Pushes full stock dataset to NewStore (`POST /api/stock_import`)

---

4. Outbound: NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC
---------------------------------------

### 4.1 Inventory Sync Process

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| API | `inventory-sync-prc-api` |
| Trigger | Scheduled every 15 minutes |
| Regions | GB (UK), AU, US |
| JIRA | ZMOBLD-262, ZAUBLD-233 |

**Flow (per region):**

DefaultnoneScheduler (every 15 min)
│
├─ 1. Read region codes from config (GB / AU / US)
├─ 2. GET all stores from NewStore
├─ 3. Filter active stores for region (exclude configured concession stores for AU/US)
├─ 4. GET all locations (stores + DCs) from NewStore
├─ 5. Filter enabled DCs from inclusion list in config
├─ 6. Build group name: {REGION}\_GROUP\_{SHA256(store\_ids + dc\_ids)}
│ Example: AU\_GROUP\_01EA7311C557C99DB4CD44C8208AB01...
├─ 7. Create/verify fulfillment location group in NewStore
│ (store group name in Anypoint Object Store)
├─ 8. GET availability\_export\_id for group
├─ 9. GET S3 URL for compressed inventory file
├─ 10. Download + decompress ZIP from S3
├─ 11. Transform: extract product\_id + qty (ATP), map store\_view by region:
│ GB → uk\_store\_view, AU → default, US → us\_store\_view
└─ 12. POST transformed payload to SFCC inventory import endpoint

### 4.2 SFCC Inventory Configuration

Each site has a dedicated inventory list referenced in `preferences.xml` (`SiteInventoryList`). All inventory list XML files live under `data/core/inventory-lists/` and are imported via the core data bundle.

ZimmermannUS and ZimmermannUSIntl share the same inventory list (`inventory_m_us`) — both sites fulfil from the same US stock pool.

| Site | Inventory List | Sync Region |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | `inventory_m_au` | AU |
| ZimmermannUK | `inventory_m_uk` | GB |
| ZimmermannUS | `inventory_m_us` | US |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | `inventory_m_us` | US (shared pool with ZimmermannUS) |
| ZimmermannEU | `inventory_m_eu` | [To be confirmed] |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | `inventory_m_eu_intl` | [To be confirmed] |
| ZimmermannHK | `inventory_m_hk` | [To be confirmed] |
| ZimmermannME | `inventory_m_me` | [To be confirmed] |

> **Note:** The current MuleSoft `inventory-sync-prc-api` syncs GB, AU, and US regions. Sync coverage for EU, EUIntl, HK, and ME is to be confirmed with the integration team.

---

5. SFCC Cartridge Touchpoints
-----------------------------

| Touchpoint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Inventory list per site | Set in `SiteInventoryList` preference in `preferences.xml` |
| Availability display | OOTB SFCC product availability checking against the per-site inventory list |
| Real-time stock for boutiques | Separate MuleSoft call via Find In Store API — see [Find In Store TSD](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292487173) |
| Inventory import | Triggered by scheduled MuleSoft job; no cartridge code required |

---

6. Error Handling & Monitoring
------------------------------

| Scenario | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Group already exists in NewStore | 409 response — compare stored group name; create new group if hash differs |
| Export job status: failed / partially\_failed | Log error; do not update Object Store last-sync date |
| Export job status: processing / waiting | Re-poll status |
| HTTP failures (any API call) | Retry up to 3 times, 1-minute interval |
| Payload failure | Automated email alert with error context |

---

7. Key Design Decisions
-----------------------

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory ownership | NewStore | OMS is the source of truth for fulfilment availability |
| Group naming | SHA256 hash of store + DC IDs | Deterministic across retries and scheduled runs; no collision risk |
| Sync frequency | Every 15 minutes | Balance between freshness and API rate limits |
| SFCC inventory model | Per-site inventory list (not shared, except US/USIntl) | Each site has different fulfilment locations and stock pools |
| US / USIntl shared inventory | Both sites use `inventory_m_us` | US domestic and US international orders fulfil from the same US stock pool |

    "content": {
      "value": "This page documents the end-to-end MuleSoft → SFCC synchronisation process for three data domains: **Product**, **Price**, and **Inventory**. All three domains share the same WebDAV-based delivery mechanism and SFCC import job pattern.

Related pages: - TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration - TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes - TSD: Price — SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e - TSD: Inventory — SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ NewStore / AP21

---

1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

AP21 is the system of record for product and price data. NewStore is the system of record for inventory availability. MuleSoft is the integration layer for all three — SFCC never connects to AP21 or NewStore directly.

All three sync domains use the same delivery pattern:

1. MuleSoft generates a domain-specific SFCC-compliant XML zip
2. MuleSoft uploads the zip to SFCC via **WebDAV** (overwriting a fixed filename in the `incoming/` folder)
3. MuleSoft triggers the SFCC import job via the **SCAPI Jobs Admin API**
4. MuleSoft polls for job completion
5. On success — zip is archived with a timestamp; on failure — zip is moved to a failed folder and an alert is raised

> **API Note:** OCAPI is deprecated. All job trigger and status poll calls use the **SCAPI Jobs Admin API** ([reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/jobs)). Authentication uses **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — not OCAPI Client ID/Secret.

| Domain | Source | MuleSoft API | SFCC Import Job | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Product | AP21 | product-prc-api | `sfcc-site-archive-import` | Event-driven (AP21 product create/update) + scheduled batch — TBC |
| Price | AP21 | product-prc-api (price feed) | `sfcc-site-archive-import` | Scheduled — full or delta — TBC |
| Inventory | NewStore | `inventory-sync-prc-api` | `sfcc-site-archive-import` | Every 15 minutes |

---

2-webdav-folder-structure2. WebDAV Folder Structure
---------------------------------------------------

SFCC exposes a WebDAV endpoint for file-based integration. MuleSoft authenticates to WebDAV using **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — the same token used for SCAPI Admin API calls.

**Base path:**

nonewide760https://{instance}.commercecloud.salesforce.com
/on/demandware.servlet/webdav/Sites/Impex/src/instance/

**Folder layout — one set per domain:**

nonewide760/Impex/src/instance/
├── product/
│ ├── incoming/
│ │ └── catalog-import.zip ← fixed filename, overwritten each run
│ ├── archive/
│ │ ├── catalog-import-20250709-143022.zip
│ │ └── catalog-import-20250708-060012.zip
│ └── failed/
│ └── catalog-import-20250707-183045.zip
│
├── price/
│ ├── incoming/
│ │ └── pricebook-import.zip ← fixed filename, overwritten each run
│ ├── archive/
│ └── failed/
│
└── inventory/
├── incoming/
│ └── inventory-import.zip ← fixed filename, overwritten each run
├── archive/
└── failed/

**Fixed filename rationale:** MuleSoft always writes the same filename to `incoming/`, overwriting the previous file. The timestamp is applied only at archive time (move from `incoming/` → `archive/` or `failed/`). This keeps the SFCC job configuration static — no dynamic file path parameter is required per execution.

---

3-sync-orchestration--mulesoft-flow-all-domains3. Sync Orchestration — MuleSoft Flow (All Domains)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following sequence applies to all three domains. Domain-specific variations are noted in Sections 4, 5, and 6.

**SCAPI Jobs Admin API base URL:**

nonewide760https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}

**Auth:**`Authorization: Bearer {amOAuth2Token}` — token obtained from Account Manager using client credentials grant.

nonewide760AP21 / NewStore (source event or scheduler trigger)
│
▼
MuleSoft
│
├── 1. GUARD CHECK
│ GET /jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions
│ ?status=Running
│ If a previous execution is running → hold; retry after interval
│ If clear → proceed
│
├── 2. GENERATE XML ZIP
│ Transform source payload → SFCC-compliant XML
│ Package as zip (see domain sections for zip contents)
│
├── 3. WEBDAV UPLOAD (overwrite)
│ PUT https://{instance}.commercecloud.salesforce.com
│ /on/demandware.servlet/webdav/Sites/Impex/src/instance/
│ {domain}/incoming/{fixed-filename}.zip
│ Overwrites any previously uploaded file
│
├── 4. TRIGGER IMPORT JOB (SCAPI Jobs Admin API)
│ POST /jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/jobs/sfcc-site-archive-import/executions
│ Headers: Authorization: Bearer {amOAuth2Token}
│ Body:
│ {
│ "parameters": [
│ { "name": "ImportFile", "value": "{domain}/incoming/{fixed-filename}.zip" },
│ { "name": "ImportMode", "value": "merge" }
│ ]
│ }
│ → returns { "id": "{executionId}", "executionStatus": "pending" }
│
├── 5. POLL JOB STATUS
│ GET /jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/jobs/sfcc-site-archive-import/executions/{executionId}
│ Poll every 10 seconds until executionStatus ≠ "running"
│
├── 6a. ON executionStatus: "finished" (exitStatus: "ok")
│ ├── Fetch BM import log from WebDAV /Impex/log/ — check for per-record errors
│ └── WebDAV MOVE {domain}/incoming/{fixed-filename}.zip
│ → {domain}/archive/{fixed-filename}-{YYYYMMDD-HHmmss}.zip
│
└── 6b. ON executionStatus: "finished" (exitStatus: "error") OR "failed"
├── WebDAV MOVE {domain}/incoming/{fixed-filename}.zip
│ → {domain}/failed/{fixed-filename}-{YYYYMMDD-HHmmss}.zip
└── Raise alert — Anypoint monitoring notification
> **Note:** SFCC does not move or clean up files on WebDAV after import. MuleSoft owns the full lifecycle — upload, trigger, archive, and cleanup.

---

4-product-sync4. Product Sync
-----------------------------

### 41-trigger4.1 Trigger

AP21 product create or update event consumed by MuleSoft, or a scheduled full/delta batch. Trigger pattern to be confirmed with MuleSoft team — see open item #1.

### 42-zip-contents4.2 Zip Contents

Product sync delivers **catalog XML only**. Pricebook XML is always delivered separately via the price sync (Section 5) — including during initial load. Both syncs run independently on their own schedules and WebDAV paths.

nonewide760catalog-import.zip
└── catalogs/
└── zimmermann-catalog/
└── catalog.xml ← master products, variants, attributes, category assignments

### 43-catalogxml-structure4.3 catalog.xml Structure

### 44-import-mode4.4 Import Mode

The catalog XML must use **merge mode** — not replace. This prevents unintended deletion of products not included in a delta feed.

xmlwide760<catalog xmlns="..." catalog-id="zimmermann-catalog">
<!-- mode="merge" is the default for catalog import — do not use mode="replace" for delta feeds -->

5-price-sync5. Price Sync
-------------------------

### 51-trigger5.1 Trigger

Scheduled — full reload or delta on price change. Runs independently from the product sync on its own schedule. Frequency and delta vs full strategy to be confirmed — see open item #2.

### 52-zip-contents5.2 Zip Contents

Price sync delivers **pricebook XML for domestic sites only**. International sites (USIntl, EUIntl, HK, ME) are served by **Global-e** which handles all currency conversion and pricing at checkout — SFCC does not hold per-currency pricebooks for those sites.

All pricebook XML files are placed inside a `pricebooks/` folder so the `sfcc-site-archive-import` job correctly identifies and processes them.

### 61-trigger6.1 Trigger

MuleSoft `inventory-sync-prc-api` runs every 15 minutes per region (AU, GB, US). EU, EUIntl, HK, ME coverage to be confirmed — see open item #3.

### 62-source6.2 Source

7-webdav-archive-strategy7. WebDAV Archive Strategy
---------------------------------------------------

| Behaviour | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Incoming filename | Fixed — `catalog-import.zip` / `pricebook-import.zip` / `inventory-import.zip` — overwritten each run |
| Timestamp applied | At archive/fail move time — not on upload |
| Archive filename pattern | `{fixed-name}-{YYYYMMDD-HHmmss}.zip` e.g. `catalog-import-20250709-143022.zip` |
| Archive on success | MuleSoft MOVE: `incoming/` → `archive/` with timestamp |
| Archive on failure | MuleSoft MOVE: `incoming/` → `failed/` with timestamp + raise alert |
| SFCC cleanup | SFCC does **not** clean up WebDAV files — MuleSoft owns full lifecycle |
| Retention | Archive and failed folders purged on a rolling 30-day window — MuleSoft scheduled cleanup job |

---

8-sfcc-import-job-configuration8. SFCC Import Job Configuration
---------------------------------------------------------------

The `sfcc-site-archive-import` system job is triggered by MuleSoft via the **SCAPI Jobs Admin API**. OCAPI is deprecated and must not be used for new integrations.

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Job ID | `sfcc-site-archive-import` |
| API | SCAPI Jobs Admin API — `POST /jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions` |
| API reference | <https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/jobs> |
| Auth | Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2) — client credentials grant. Registered in Account Manager, **not** in BM OCAPI settings |
| Base URL | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/jobs/v1/organizations/{organizationId}` |
| Guard check | `GET .../jobs/sfcc-site-archive-import/executions?status=Running` — before every upload |
| Job trigger | `POST .../jobs/sfcc-site-archive-import/executions` with `ImportFile` and `ImportMode` parameters |
| Status poll | `GET .../jobs/sfcc-site-archive-import/executions/{executionId}` — poll until `executionStatus` ≠ `"running"` |
| Success condition | `executionStatus: "finished"` + `exitStatus: "ok"` |
| Failure condition | `executionStatus: "finished"` + `exitStatus: "error"`, or `executionStatus: "failed"` |
| BM import log | `GET` from WebDAV `/Impex/log/` after job completion — required to detect per-record errors when job-level status is `ok` |
| Job configuration | BM → Administration → Operations → Jobs |

> **Important:** SFCC job status reflects job-level outcome only. A job can return `exitStatus: "ok"` while individual product or price records fail validation. MuleSoft **must** fetch and parse the BM import log after every successful job execution to detect partial failures.

---

9-error-handling9. Error Handling
---------------------------------

| Scenario | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Previous job still running | SCAPI guard check before upload — hold and retry; do not overwrite `incoming/` until clear |
| WebDAV upload failure | MuleSoft retries up to 3 times with 30-second interval; raises alert on persistent failure |
| Job trigger failure (SCAPI error) | MuleSoft retries up to 3 times; raises alert — file remains in `incoming/` for manual replay |
| Job exitStatus: error / failed | MuleSoft moves zip to `failed/` with timestamp; raises alert via Anypoint monitoring |
| Job ok but log contains record errors | MuleSoft parses BM log; raises alert listing failed product/price/inventory IDs |
| Corrupt or invalid XML | SFCC job fails immediately; MuleSoft catches via failed status; zip moved to `failed/` |
| Archive folder full / WebDAV quota | Retention cleanup job prevents accumulation; monitored via Anypoint |

> **Owner:** Integration Lead
> **Last updated:** June 2026
> **Registry entry:** [05.5 — Agent Registry](../278921217)

---

1. Purpose & Scope
------------------

This TSD describes the architecture, component boundaries, and governance constraints for the AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent — a hybrid agent that automates defect classification and fix-branch creation following failed BrowserStack Automate runs on the Zimmermann SFCC replatform programme.

**In scope:**
- CI-automated triage pipeline (GitHub Actions + AWS Bedrock)
- Tier classification logic and routing decisions
- Automated Jira defect creation and GitHub fix-branch creation
- Claude Code CLI skill for interactive investigation and fix on Tier 1/2 defects
- Security boundaries, credential handling, and hard stops

**Out of scope:**
- BrowserStack Automate configuration (covered in [Guide 3](../../277807105/277676053))
- Zephyr Scale result sync (covered in Guide 3)
- The Playwright spec authoring workflow (covered in Guide 3)
- PR merge — this always requires a human reviewer

---

2. Solution Overview
--------------------

The agent operates as a **hybrid** — a CI-automated layer handles triage and administration for all failures without any human present, and an interactive Claude Code CLI skill handles investigation and fix for Tier 1/2 defects when a developer picks up the Jira ticket.

The split is designed around risk. Tier 3/4 files are squad-owned and feature-scoped — the blast radius of an incorrect automated fix is contained and reviewable via PR. Tier 1/2 files affect all storefronts and multiple squads — automated code generation on those files introduces unacceptable risk, so the agent stops at investigation and a developer owns the fix.

```
BrowserStack run completes (failures detected)
          │
          ▼
CI: GitHub Actions — defect-triage.yml
          │
          ├── Bedrock (Haiku): classify each failure
          │   code defect / env issue / test data
          │
          ├── CODEOWNERS check: determine file tier
          │   (deterministic — not delegated to LLM)
          │
          ├── Jira REST API: create defect ticket (all tiers, all classifications)
          │
          └── Route by tier
                │
                ├── Tier 3/4 code defect
                │   ├── Bedrock (Sonnet): investigate + generate fix
                │   ├── GitHub: create fix branch with code change
                │   └── GitHub: raise PR (human review required)
                │
                ├── Tier 1/2 code defect
                │   ├── Bedrock (Sonnet): investigate, produce root cause analysis
                │   ├── GitHub: create fix branch (investigation notes only, no code)
                │   └── Jira ticket pre-populated with RCA — assigned to Lead Dev (T1) or Squad Lead (T2)
                │         │
                │         ▼
                │   Developer picks up ticket, runs /defect-triage [JIRA-KEY]
                │   Claude Code CLI skill pulls context via MCP, works interactively
                │
                └── Env / test data issue (all tiers)
                    └── Jira ticket raised and assigned — no branch created
```

---

3. Component Architecture
-------------------------

The agent has four components. Each has a single responsibility and a defined owner.

| Component | Location | Responsibility | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CI workflow** | `.github/workflows/defect-triage.yml` | Orchestrates the pipeline — triggers on BrowserStack failure, calls the Bedrock invocation script, drives Jira writes via the Jira REST API and GitHub actions via the GitHub API | Integration Lead |
| **Bedrock invocation script** | `scripts/agents/defect-triage/bedrock-invoke.js` | Node.js script called by the CI workflow. Builds the prompt, calls AWS Bedrock, parses the response, returns structured JSON to the workflow | Integration Lead |
| **CODEOWNERS tier classifier** | `scripts/agents/defect-triage/classify-tier.js` | Deterministic script — reads the affected file paths from the failure report and cross-references against CODEOWNERS to output a tier classification. No LLM involvement. | Integration Lead |
| **Claude Code CLI skill** | `.claude/skills/defect-triage.md` | Interactive skill invoked by a developer on Tier 1/2 defects. Pulls Jira ticket context and investigation notes via the Atlassian MCP, checks out the pre-created fix branch, and guides the developer through the fix session. | Lead Developer |

> **Note on MCP vs REST API boundary:** The Atlassian MCP is only available in interactive Claude Desktop sessions — it cannot be called from a GitHub Actions runner. All Jira writes from the CI workflow use the Jira REST API directly with a scoped service account token. The Atlassian MCP is used only by the Claude Code CLI skill in interactive developer sessions.

---

4. Tier Classification & Routing Logic
--------------------------------------

Tier classification is **always deterministic**. The LLM is never asked to decide which tier a file belongs to — that decision is made by `classify-tier.js` reading CODEOWNERS. This is a hard architectural constraint: allowing the LLM to self-classify would create a path for the agent to incorrectly escalate its own permissions.

```
Affected file paths extracted from BrowserStack failure report
          │
          ▼
classify-tier.js reads CODEOWNERS
          │
          ├── Tier 1 match → hard stop on code generation
          │   (design tokens, shared hooks, runtime config, CI workflows)
          │
          ├── Tier 2 match → investigation only, no code write
          │   (global shell components, shared product components, hooks with 5+ consumers)
          │
          ├── Tier 3 match → automated fix permitted
          │   (squad-owned components)
          │
          └── Tier 4 match → automated fix permitted
              (feature-scoped files)
```

**Routing matrix by failure classification and tier:**

| Classification | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Code defect | Jira ticket + RCA + fix branch (notes only) → developer runs `/defect-triage` | Jira ticket + RCA + fix branch (notes only) + Tier 2 label → developer runs `/defect-triage` | Jira ticket + RCA + fix branch with code + PR (auto-fix) | Jira ticket + RCA + fix branch with code + PR (auto-fix) |
| Environment issue | Jira ticket → assigned to relevant team | Jira ticket → assigned to relevant team | Jira ticket → assigned to relevant team | Jira ticket → assigned to relevant team |
| Test data issue | Jira ticket → assigned to fixture owner | Jira ticket → assigned to fixture owner | Jira ticket → assigned to fixture owner | Jira ticket → assigned to fixture owner |

---

5. AWS Bedrock Integration
--------------------------

All LLM calls use **AWS Bedrock**, not the Anthropic API directly. This is a programme-wide constraint — see the [Agent Registry](../278921217) governance principles.

### 5.1 Model Selection

| Task | Model | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Failure classification (code defect / env issue / test data) | Claude Haiku on Bedrock | Low-complexity structured classification. Fast and cost-efficient for high-volume CI runs. |
| Root cause investigation | Claude Sonnet on Bedrock | Requires reasoning across stack traces, file contents, and test case context. Sonnet's reasoning capability justifies the higher cost at this step. |
| Fix generation (Tier 3/4) | Claude Sonnet on Bedrock | Code generation quality matters — Haiku is not used for any code write step. |

### 5.2 Invocation Pattern

The Bedrock invocation script (`bedrock-invoke.js`) uses the AWS SDK v3 `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` package. It does not use any Anthropic SDK — all calls go through the Bedrock `InvokeModel` endpoint.

```
// bedrock-invoke.js — simplified structure
import { BedrockRuntimeClient, InvokeModelCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime'

const client = new BedrockRuntimeClient({ region: process.env.AWS_BEDROCK_REGION })

export async function classify(failureReport) {
  const command = new InvokeModelCommand({
    modelId: 'anthropic.claude-haiku-20240307-v1:0',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      anthropic_version: 'bedrock-2023-05-31',
      max_tokens: 512,
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: buildClassificationPrompt(failureReport) }]
    }),
    contentType: 'application/json',
    accept: 'application/json'
  })
  const response = await client.send(command)
  return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(response.body))
}

export async function investigate(failureReport, fileContents, testCaseDetail) {
  const command = new InvokeModelCommand({
    modelId: 'anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      anthropic_version: 'bedrock-2023-05-31',
      max_tokens: 4096,
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: buildInvestigationPrompt(failureReport, fileContents, testCaseDetail) }]
    }),
    contentType: 'application/json',
    accept: 'application/json'
  })
  const response = await client.send(command)
  return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(response.body))
}
```

### 5.3 Credential Handling

AWS credentials are stored as GitHub Actions secrets and injected as environment variables into the CI job. They are never logged, never passed in LLM prompts, and never committed to source control.

| Secret | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | Bedrock IAM access key |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Bedrock IAM secret |
| `AWS_BEDROCK_REGION` | AWS region hosting the Bedrock endpoint (e.g. `us-east-1`) |

### 5.4 IAM Boundary

The IAM role used by the CI job must be scoped to the minimum permissions required:

* `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the specific model ARNs used (Haiku and Sonnet)
* No `bedrock:ListFoundationModels`, no `bedrock:CreateModelCustomizationJob`
* No access to any other AWS service from this role

---

6. GitHub Actions Workflow Design
---------------------------------

### 6.1 Trigger

The `defect-triage.yml` workflow triggers on completion of the BrowserStack execution job in `qa.yml`, conditional on failures being present:

```
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['BrowserStack E2E']
    types: [completed]

jobs:
  triage:
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' }}
```

### 6.2 Job Structure

```
jobs:
  parse-failures        # Extract failed test names, file paths, BrowserStack session URLs
  classify-tier         # Run classify-tier.js — deterministic CODEOWNERS check
  classify-failures     # Call Bedrock Haiku — code defect / env / test data per failure
  create-jira-defects   # Jira REST API — one Jira ticket per failure (service account token)
  investigate           # Call Bedrock Sonnet — RCA for code defects
  create-branches       # GitHub API — fix branch per code defect
  generate-fix          # Bedrock Sonnet — code fix for Tier 3/4 only
  raise-prs             # GitHub API — PR per Tier 3/4 fix branch
```

`classify-tier` and `classify-failures` run in parallel after `parse-failures` completes. All downstream jobs depend on both completing.

### 6.3 Jira REST API Integration

Jira defects are created using the Jira REST API v3 with a scoped service account token. The service account must have issue creation and linking permissions in the SFCC project only — no broader Jira access.

```
// jira-create-issue.js — simplified structure
export async function createDefect(payload) {
  const response = await fetch(
    'https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue',
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(
          `${process.env.JIRA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}:${process.env.JIRA_API_TOKEN}`
        ).toString('base64')}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload)
    }
  )
  return response.json()
}
```

Additional GitHub Actions secrets required for Jira integration:

| Secret | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `JIRA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` | Email of the Jira service account used by the CI workflow |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN` | Jira API token scoped to issue create and link in the SFCC project |

### 6.4 Jira Defect Content

Each Jira defect created by the agent is pre-populated with:

* **Summary:** `[STORY-KEY] [Test Case Name] — [Classification] — [Browser / Storefront]`
* **Description:** failure message, stack trace, BrowserStack session recording link, root cause analysis (Sonnet output), affected file paths and their tier
* **Labels:** `agent-raised`, `defect`, the classification, the storefront, the file tier
* **Priority:** P1 if the failure blocks story sign-off; P2 otherwise
* **Assignee:** Lead Developer (Tier 1), Squad Lead (Tier 2), unassigned (Tier 3/4 — PR raised instead)
* **Linked to:** the originating Jira story and the Zephyr test case

### 6.5 Fix Branch Naming

| Tier | Branch name |
| --- | --- |
| Tier 1/2 (investigation only) | `fix/agent-investigation-[STORY-KEY]-TC-[N]-[short-description]` |
| Tier 3/4 (auto-fix) | `fix/agent-autofix-[STORY-KEY]-TC-[N]-[short-description]` |

The `agent-investigation` vs `agent-autofix` prefix makes branch intent visible at a glance in the GitHub branch list and in PR titles.

---

7. Claude Code CLI Skill Design
-------------------------------

### 7.1 Purpose

The `/defect-triage [JIRA-KEY]` skill is invoked by a developer when they pick up a Tier 1/2 defect Jira ticket. It provides a structured, context-loaded starting point for the interactive fix session — removing the setup overhead of manually finding the failure detail, checking out the branch, and reading the investigation notes.

### 7.2 What the Skill Does on Invocation

```
Developer runs: /defect-triage ZIM-DEF-089
          │
          ▼
Skill reads JIRA-KEY from the command argument
          │
          ▼
Atlassian MCP: retrieve the Jira defect ticket
— failure detail, stack trace, BrowserStack session link
— RCA from the CI investigation step
— affected file paths and tier classification
— linked Jira story and Zephyr test case
          │
          ▼
GitHub MCP: check out the pre-created fix branch
fix/agent-investigation-[STORY-KEY]-TC-[N]-[description]
          │
          ▼
Skill presents a structured session brief to the developer:
— Summary of the failure
— The RCA the CI agent produced
— The files involved and their tier
— A proposed investigation approach
— Explicit note: "This is a Tier [1/2] file —
  you own the fix. I will assist but will not write
  to this file without your explicit instruction."
          │
          ▼
Developer works interactively with Claude Code to
investigate, implement a fix, and raise a PR
```

### 7.3 Skill Constraints

The skill observes the same tier rules as the CI agent:

* Tier 1 files: Claude Code will analyse and propose a fix approach, but will not write to the file without the developer typing an explicit instruction to do so
* Tier 2 files: Claude Code will implement a fix on developer instruction; the PR it raises will automatically carry the Tier 2 label and request a second reviewer
* The skill will not suppress the tier warning or proceed past it silently

---

8. Security & Guardrails
------------------------

| Guardrail | Enforcement mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| No auto-merge | GitHub branch protection on `develop` and `release/**` — cannot be bypassed by any workflow or bot |
| Tier 1 hard stop on code generation | `classify-tier.js` outputs tier before any Bedrock call; CI job conditional blocks fix generation step for Tier 1 |
| Tier 2 auto-fix permitted but labelled | PR carries `tier-2-change` label; CODEOWNERS enforces second reviewer requirement |
| No LLM tier classification | `classify-tier.js` is a deterministic CODEOWNERS lookup — not a Bedrock call |
| Credentials never in LLM context | Bedrock and Jira credentials injected as CI environment variables; prompt construction never includes credential values |
| Agent-raised PRs are identifiable | All agent PRs carry the `agent-raised` label; branch name prefix `fix/agent-` is enforced in the workflow |
| Jira writes use a scoped service account | The CI workflow Jira service account has issue create and link permissions only — no admin, no bulk operations, no other projects |
| CodeRabbit reviews agent PRs | `.coderabbit.yaml` applies the same review rules to agent-raised PRs as to human-raised PRs — assertive profile, tier warnings, test coverage checks |

---

9. Open Decisions
-----------------

| # | Decision | Status | Resolution | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OD-01 | AWS Bedrock region | 🔴 Open | `us-east-1` (lowest latency to GitHub Actions runners) vs `ap-southeast-2` (closer to Zimmermann AU operations) | Integration Lead |
| OD-02 | IAM role provisioning | 🔴 Open | Zimmermann IT provisions the IAM role and delivers credentials to Accenture as GitHub secrets, vs Accenture provisions under a temporary sandbox account | Zimmermann IT + Integration Lead |
| OD-03 | Jira writes in CI context — MCP vs REST API | ✅ Resolved | The Atlassian MCP requires a persistent Claude Desktop session and cannot be called from a GitHub Actions runner. **Decision: CI workflow uses the Jira REST API v3 with a scoped service account token for all automated Jira writes. The Atlassian MCP is used only by the `/defect-triage` Claude Code CLI skill in interactive developer sessions.** Registry governance principle updated to reflect this boundary. | Integration Lead |
| OD-04 | Sonnet model version on Bedrock | 🔴 Open | Confirm which Claude Sonnet version is available in the selected Bedrock region and whether it requires a provisioned throughput commitment at expected CI run volumes | Integration Lead |
| OD-05 | P1 vs P2 severity assignment logic | 🔴 Open | Proposal: P1 if the failing test case is tagged Critical or High priority in Zephyr; P2 otherwise | Lead QA + Integration Lead |

---

    "content": {
      "value": "1. Overview
-----------

The order domain covers three distinct flows in the Zimmermann SFCC platform:

| Flow | Direction | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Order | SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore | Customer places order on SFCC; MuleSoft creates it in NewStore OMS |
| Order History & Details | SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore | My Account — historic orders, returns, and order detail retrieval |
| Returns (Store → Narvar) | NewStore → MuleSoft → Narvar | Store return processed; linked to Narvar tracking |
| Returns (Narvar → 3PL) | Narvar → MuleSoft → 3PL SFTP | Customer-initiated return; MuleSoft routes to 3PL |

---

2. Flow: Create Order
---------------------

### 2.1 Trigger

A customer completes checkout on SFCC. SFCC calls MuleSoft with the **order ID** only — MuleSoft fetches the full order detail from SFCC.

### 2.2 System Flow

nonewide760Customer places order on SFCC
│
SFCC ──[orderId]──► orders-prc-api (Experience API)
│
Fetch full order from SFCC API
│
Transform to NewStore schema
(see mapping rules below)
│
POST ──► NewStore (create order)
│
Response ──► SFCC (order\_id + success/fail)

### 2.3 Key Data Mapping Rules

| Rule | Logic |
| --- | --- |
| Item quantity | SFCC qty > 1 split into individual line items (NewStore has no qty field) |
| 0-value orders (rewards) | Payment array → blank; shipping discount applied at item level |
| Price | From `extension_attributes.price` (SFCC recalculated field) |
| Tax (no rewards) | `item_tax_amount ÷ quantity` |
| Tax (with rewards) | `tax_pct × (price − discounts − rewards)` |
| Discount | `total_discount ÷ quantity` |
| Rewards split | `((item_price − item_discount) × total_rewards) ÷ (subtotal + order_discount)` |
| Rounding | Discrepancies adjusted on last item; final reconciliation on last product's price |
| Reward application order | Apply to items first, then to shipping |

### 2.4 SFCC Cartridge Touchpoint

* Custom controller/script in `int_custom_zim_global` calls MuleSoft `orders-prc-api` after order placement
* Passes `orderId` as query parameter
* Handles success/failure response and surfaces error to checkout if needed

---

3. Flow: Order History & Details (My Account)
---------------------------------------------

### 3.1 Trigger

Customer navigates to My Account in SFCC. SFCC calls MuleSoft to retrieve order data from NewStore.

### 3.2 System Flow

nonewide760SFCC (My Account)
│
├──[GET /orders?customer\_id&offset&count]──► sfcc-exp-api ──► NewStore
│ │
│ order summaries
│
├──[GET /orders/{order\_id}?id\_type=internal]──► sfcc-exp-api ──► NewStore
│ │
│ full order + payments + fulfilment
│
└──[GET /returns?customer\_id&offset&count]──► sfcc-exp-api ──► NewStore
│
return summaries

### 3.3 API Endpoints (SFCC calls these)

| Operation | Dev URL | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Historic Orders | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-dev/api/orders?customer_id={id}&offset={n}&count={n}` | GET |
| Order Details | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-dev/api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | GET |
| Returns | `https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api-dev/api/returns?customer_id={id}&offset={n}&count={n}` | GET |

### 3.4 Response Data Model (from NewStore)

**Order summary fields returned to SFCC:**

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | NewStore order ID (e.g., ZX00000339) |
| `placed_at` | ISO timestamp |
| `status` | closed / open / cancelled |
| `currency` | Site currency (GBP / AUD / USD / EUR) |
| `fulfillment_type` | in\_store\_purchase / ship\_to\_address |
| `items[].product_attributes` | name, size, color, image\_url |
| `items[].external_identifier` | sku, ean13 |
| `items[].extended_attributes` | Collection, Material, Sleeve (display metadata) |
| `totals` | gross, net, tax, discount, shipping |
| `payments` | psp, method, amount, status |

---

4. Flow: Returns
----------------

### 4.1 Store Return → Narvar

nonewide760NewStore (return.processed webhook)
──► orders-prc-api
──► Narvar (return linked in tracking portal)

### 4.2 Narvar → 3PL

nonewide760Narvar (return\_initiated\_standard event)
──► orders-prc-api
──► 3PL SFTP (return label + item data)
──► Narvar S3 (cache, 60-day retention)

---

5. SFCC Cartridge Touchpoints
-----------------------------

| Page / Feature | Integration Point |
| --- | --- |
| Checkout (order confirmation) | POST to `orders-prc-api` with orderId |
| My Account → Order History | GET `sfcc-exp-api` /orders |
| My Account → Order Detail | GET `sfcc-exp-api` /orders/{id} |
| My Account → Returns | GET `sfcc-exp-api` /returns |

All calls authenticated via client credentials stored in SFCC custom site preferences or SFCC secrets management. MuleSoft uses Mule secure property placeholder for credentials.

---

6. Error Handling
-----------------

| HTTP Status | Scenario | SFCC Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Success | Render order data |
| 400 | Invalid request | Log + surface error message |
| 401 | Unauthorised | Re-authenticate + retry once |
| 404 | Order / customer not found | Show empty state in My Account |
| 500 | MuleSoft internal error | Show generic error; alert via Anypoint |

MuleSoft retries: 3 attempts, 1-minute interval.

---

7. Key Design Decisions
-----------------------

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
