I've now read all nine TSDs in full (or via their cross-references). Here's the in-depth analysis, grouped by the three distinct genres I found — then one question before I write the template.

## In-depth analysis

### Genre A — Broad Architecture TSD
**[Technical Solution Design – PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)** (mirrored at [.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md](.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md))

- **Approach:** Top-down. Establishes the whole technical foundation once so per-feature TSDs don't re-litigate it. Explicitly defers functional/per-vendor detail out of scope.
- **Structure:** `Purpose & Scope` (explicit in/out-scope lists) → `Solution Overview` (ASCII architecture diagram + boundary legend) → `Frontend Stack` → `Customisation Model` → `Multi-Site/Locale` → `Checkout Ownership` → `Integration Map` (a 5-class boundary model + master table + non-system stakeholders) → `SSR/SEO/GEO` → `Performance` → `Accessibility` → `Consent & Marketing` → `Graceful Degradation` (+ blast-radius containment) → `Testing Strategy` → `CI/CD & Environments`.
- **Foundation:** Requirement-ID traceability throughout (`DMU-030`, `REG-041`, `PRC-34..43`), boundary/ownership as the organising spine, "why" baked in beside each "what", tables + ASCII diagrams, Australian spelling.

### Genre B — Domain / Integration TSDs (the dominant family, 5–7 of 9)
[Product — Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208) · [Price — Pricebooks & Global-e](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292388871) · [Inventory](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292749334) · [Orders](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061187) · [Catalogue Sync](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) · [SCAPI Admin (Alt Pattern)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/315490342) · [Product Attributes](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312377345)

- **Approach:** Data-flow-first. Each opens by naming the **system of record** and the **integration-layer boundary** ("AP21 is SoR; MuleSoft is the integration layer; SFCC never connects directly"), then documents the pipeline end-to-end.
- **Structure — a near-identical skeleton:**
  1. `Overview` (SoR + boundary statement)
  2. `Architecture / End-to-End Data Flow` (ASCII diagram)
  3. Domain-specific sections (catalogue structure / pricebook register / sync orchestration / flow-by-flow, with XML samples, folder layouts, endpoint tables)
  4. `SFCC Cartridge / System Touchpoints`
  5. `Error Handling & Monitoring`
  6. **`Key Design Decisions`** — table of `Decision | Choice | Rationale`
  7. **`Open Items`** — table of `# | Item | Owner | Status`
  8. Cross-links to sibling TSDs
- **Foundation:** Heavy on registers/mapping tables, concrete IDs (JIRA `ZMOBLD-263`, pricebook IDs, API names), explicit config file references (`preferences.xml`), and "TBC + owner" markers for anything unconfirmed. Product Attributes is a lighter **reference-data child** (pure mapping tables); SCAPI-Admin is an **alternative-pattern** variant that deliberately mirrors the Catalogue Sync section order for direct comparison.

### Genre C — Component / Agent TSD
**[AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277708843)**

- **Approach:** Component-design + governance. Documents a buildable system's boundaries and — critically — its *risk controls*, with design rationale framed around blast radius.
- **Structure:** metadata header (`Status / Owner / Last updated / Registry entry`) → `Purpose & Scope` (in/out) → `Solution Overview` (diagram + risk reasoning) → `Component Architecture` (`Component | Location | Responsibility | Owner`) → logic sections (classification, routing matrix) → integration specifics (Bedrock, model selection, **credential handling**, IAM boundary — with code snippets) → workflow/skill design → **`Security & Guardrails`** (`Guardrail | Enforcement mechanism`) → `Open Decisions` (`# | Decision | Status | Resolution | Owner`) → programme-attribution footer.
- **Foundation:** Same DNA as Genre B (design-decisions table, open-items table, ownership, diagrams) but adds a **status header**, a dedicated **security/guardrails** section, and **code snippets**.

### Common DNA across all nine (the template's mandatory core)
1. **Overview** stating system-of-record / boundary / what-owns-what
2. Explicit **In-scope / Out-of-scope** (on the broader ones)
3. At least one **diagram** (ASCII data-flow or architecture)
4. **Tables** as the default medium (registers, mappings, config)
5. **Key Design Decisions** — `Decision | Choice | Rationale`
6. **Error handling / graceful degradation**
7. **Open Items / Open Decisions** — `# | Item | Owner | Status` (always closing)
8. **Cross-links** to related TSDs
9. **Requirement-ID / JIRA traceability** and **per-item ownership**
10. **Security/credential handling** where relevant; **Australian spelling** throughout

---

Before I write the file, one genuine fork changes the deliverable. Everything else I'll default sensibly: place it at `.docs/templates/tsd-template.md`, portable Markdown (works in-repo and pasted into Confluence), Australian spelling, requirement-ID + ownership + open-items scaffolding retained, with `<!-- guidance -->` comments and `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` fields.

# TSD Templates

Templates for authoring a **Technical Solution Document (TSD)** for the Zimmermann SFCC / PWA
programme. Derived from the existing TSD corpus in the SFCC Confluence space so a new TSD reads
like the ones already signed off — same section order, same "why" tables, same open-items
discipline.

## Pick the right template

| Template | Use when the TSD describes… | Modelled on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tsd-integration-template.md`](./tsd-integration-template.md) | A **data domain or integration pipeline** — how data flows between systems, who owns it, and how it syncs. The most common kind. | Product · Price · Inventory · Orders · Catalogue Sync |
| [`tsd-architecture-template.md`](./tsd-architecture-template.md) | A **broad architectural foundation** spanning stack, multi-site, integrations, SSR/SEO, performance, testing, and CI/CD. Usually one per platform/programme. | Technical Solution Design – PWA |
| [`tsd-component-template.md`](./tsd-component-template.md) | A **buildable component, service, or agent** with defined component boundaries, credentials, and governance/guardrails. | AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent |

When a doc spans two genres (e.g. a component that is mostly an integration pipeline), start
from the closest-fit template and pull the extra sections you need from the others.

## Conventions shared by all three

These are the "TSD DNA" every existing Zimmermann TSD follows — the templates bake them in, but
keep them in mind while filling one out:

1. **Open with boundaries.** State the system of record, the integration layer, and what each
   system does *not* do ("SFCC never connects to AP21 directly"). Ambiguity here is the most
   expensive kind.
2. **Say what's out of scope**, not just what's in — the broader the TSD, the more this matters.
3. **At least one diagram.** An ASCII data-flow / architecture sketch beats prose for boundaries.
   Link a Confluence whiteboard for anything richer.
4. **Tables are the default medium** — registers, mappings, endpoint lists, config.
5. **Capture the *why*, not just the *what*** — every TSD ends with a `Key Design Decisions`
   table (`Decision | Choice | Rationale`).
6. **Every unknown is a tracked open item** with an owner and a status — never a silent
   assumption. Mark inline unknowns `[TBC — owner]`.
7. **Trace to requirements / tickets** — reference functional-requirement IDs (`DMU-030`,
   `REG-041`, `PRC-34`, `CFD-023`) and JIRA keys (`SFCC-123`, `ZMOBLD-263`) wherever a claim maps
   to one.
8. **Cross-link related TSDs** rather than duplicating their content.
9. **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored prose (`catalogue`, `colour`, `localisation`,
   `organisation`). Keep upstream Salesforce identifiers verbatim.
10. **Security where relevant** — never document a real secret; describe credential *boundaries*
    (where a token lives, what it can do, that it is never logged).

## How to use

1. Copy the chosen template to its home — a new Confluence page under
   [05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577731),
   or `.docs/` if it belongs in-repo.
2. Replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`.
3. Delete `<!-- guidance -->` comments and any optional section that doesn't apply — an empty
   section is worse than no section.
4. Leave the `Open Items` table in place even at sign-off; a TSD with zero open items is rare and
   usually means something wasn't interrogated.

message.content: what is the difference between a TSD and a TDD?

content.thinking: The user is asking about the distinction between a TSD and a TDD in the context of the Zimmermann project. TSD stands for Technical Solution Document or Technical Solution Design, which we've been working with. TDD most likely refers to Technical Design Document here, though it could also mean Test-Driven Development—but given our focus on technical documentation, the former interpretation makes more sense. A TSD describes the solution architecture—what systems integrate and how they connect at a high level, with design decisions and trade-offs—while a TDD goes deeper into implementation details like specific APIs, schemas, and code-level design that developers actually build from. The flow goes from requirements through the TSD's architectural blueprint down to the TDD's granular specifications.

content.text:
Good question — and worth pinning down, because "TDD" has two common meanings. In the context we've been working in (documents), it's almost certainly **Technical Design Document**, so I'll lead with that, then flag the other meaning.

## TSD vs TDD (as documents)

Both sit between requirements and code, but at different altitudes:

| | **TSD** — Technical Solution Document/Design | **TDD** — Technical Design Document |
|---|---|---|
| **Altitude** | Solution / architecture level | Component / implementation level |
| **Answers** | *How do we solve this, across systems?* | *How is this specific piece built?* |
| **Content** | Systems involved, integrations, data flows, ownership boundaries, key design decisions & trade-offs, open items | Module/class structure, API contracts, data schemas, sequence diagrams, function signatures, error handling at code level |
| **Audience** | Architects, leads, integration team, stakeholders | The developer(s) building it |
| **Scope** | Broad — often one per domain or platform | Narrow — one per feature/component |

**The chain:** PRD/BRD (business + functional requirements) → **TSD** (solution architecture) → **TDD** (detailed component design) → code + tests.

### How it maps to what we just built
The three templates are all **TSDs** — solution-level. They say things like "Contentful owns editorial content via the Delivery API; product data stays in SFCC via AP21→MuleSoft," and capture *design decisions* and *boundaries*.

A **TDD** for the same Contentful work would go a level deeper: the exact content-type field schemas, the specific React components/hooks that render each type, the `contentful` SDK client config, the cache-purge webhook handler signature, retry/error logic per call. In this repo, much of what would traditionally be a TDD actually lives *as the code itself* + the `.claude/rules/` conventions + Storybook/Vitest — the codebase is the detailed design, so the project leans on TSDs and doesn't formally produce separate TDDs.

## The other meaning
**TDD** far more often means **Test-Driven Development** — the practice of writing a failing test *before* the implementation (red → green → refactor). That's a *workflow*, not a document, and it's relevant here too: this project runs Vitest / Storybook `play` / Playwright, and there's even a `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill available. Different thing entirely from a Technical Design Document — same acronym.

If you meant Test-Driven Development rather than the document, say so and I'll go into how it'd apply to the Zimmermann test layers.

content.text:
Tim's feedback reframes what a TSD *is* here — not "document a domain/system," but "state one problem and its solution, nothing else." My templates were reverse-engineered from the existing Confluence corpus, which is broad; Tim is telling us the corpus is heavier than a TSD should be. Here's the audit and the revision plan.

---

## 1. The principle shift

| | Templates as built | Tim's definition |
|---|---|---|
| Organising question | "Document this domain/system" | "What problem are we solving, and how?" |
| Scope | Broad — a whole domain or platform | Narrow — one problem (e.g. *"Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"*) |
| Everything else | Embedded as sections | Linked out as context, not embedded |

His three lines, distilled: **problem → solution is the whole doc.** Registers, monitoring, performance, testing, CI/CD, governance — "all the other stuff" — either belongs to the solution directly or gets a link, not a section.

A sharp knock-on: his example is *far* narrower than SFCC-123's title ("Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model"). By his definition SFCC-123 isn't one TSD — it's several small ones (conditional-rendering-via-SFCC-IDs, each content type's model, locale bootstrap…). TSDs get smaller and more numerous.

## 2. Audit — what survives the "problem/solution only" test

**Verdict legend:** ✅ keep (problem/solution core) · ✂️ cut ("the other stuff") · ↩️ demote to a link/one-liner (context)

### Integration template
| Section | Verdict | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Overview (SoR + boundary) | ✅ → rename **Problem / Context** | The boundary *frames* the problem; keep it, but lead with the problem. |
| End-to-End Data Flow | ✅ | Scoped to the problem, this *is* the solution shape. |
| Domain structure (registers/mappings) | ✂️ | Reference data, not a solution — unless the specific mapping *is* the fix. |
| Sync/Flow process | ✅ | Keep when it's the solution mechanism. |
| System touchpoints | ↩️ | Only the touchpoints the solution changes. |
| Error handling & **monitoring** | ↩️ | Keep failure handling intrinsic to the solution; drop general monitoring. |
| Key Design Decisions | ✅ | Core — the "why" of the solution. |
| Open Items | ✅ | Tracked unknowns. |
| Related TSDs | ✅ | This is the "link out" mechanism. |

### Architecture template
| Section | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Stack · Multi-site · Integration Map · SSR/SEO · Performance · A11y · Consent · Graceful Degradation · Testing · CI/CD | ✂️ **all of it** |

This template is **"all the other stuff" by definition** — it's a platform *reference*, not a problem/solution. Verdict: **retire it as a TSD template.**

### Component/agent template
| Section | Verdict | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose & Scope | ✅ → **Problem** | Slim to the problem. |
| Solution Overview | ✅ | Core. |
| Component Architecture | ✅ | Keep when the solution has multiple parts. |
| Core logic | ✅ | This is the solution. |
| Integrations / Credential / **IAM boundary** | ↩️ | Keep only credential boundaries the solution introduces; full IAM is "other stuff." |
| Workflow / Interface | ✅ | Keep when it's the solution. |
| **Security & Guardrails** | ✂️ | Governance — cut unless the problem *is* a security control. |
| Open Decisions | ✅ | Keep. |

## 3. Planned revisions

**R1 — Consolidate 3 templates → 1 lean TSD template.** The genre split was largely driven by "the other stuff" (the architecture genre existed only to hold it; the component genre's distinctiveness was governance). Once that's cut, the three collapse to one spine. *Justification: matches "only addressing the problem/solution"; less to maintain; every TSD reads the same.*

**New spine (what Tim keeps — pointed and structured):**
```
TSD: <the specific problem>
  Status · Owner · Date            (one line)
  1. Problem / Context             (what we're solving + the one constraint/boundary that matters)

# TSD Templates

Templates for authoring a **Technical Solution Document (TSD)** for the Zimmermann SFCC / PWA
programme. Derived from the existing TSD corpus in the SFCC Confluence space, refined against the
project lead's guidance.

## The one rule (per Tim)

> **A TSD addresses one problem and its solution — nothing else.**
> *"It only needs to be addressing the problem/solution. Not all the other stuff."*

Every section in every template must advance **problem → solution**. If a section doesn't, delete
it. **Link** context (architecture, requirements, sibling TSDs) rather than reproducing it. If
you're describing a *domain or system* instead of *solving a problem*, you've picked the wrong
altitude — go narrower.

## Pick the right template

| Template | Use when the problem is… | Modelled on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tsd-problem-solution-template.md`](./tsd-problem-solution-template.md) | **A single, concrete problem** — a behaviour, config, or rendering outcome. The default and most common. e.g. *"Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"*. | Tim's definition |
| [`tsd-integration-template.md`](./tsd-integration-template.md) | **Data moving correctly across systems** — a pipeline with a source of record and an integration layer. | Product · Price · Inventory · Orders · Catalogue Sync |
| [`tsd-architecture-template.md`](./tsd-architecture-template.md) | **A platform foundation** that must be fixed before feature work. Usually one per platform. | Technical Solution Design – PWA |
| [`tsd-component-template.md`](./tsd-component-template.md) | **Building a component/service/agent safely** — with component boundaries and (often) governance. | AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent |

**When in doubt, start with `tsd-problem-solution-template.md`.** Reach for one of the other three
only when the problem genuinely needs a cross-system flow map, a platform-wide foundation, or
component/governance structure. Splitting a broad brief (e.g. a whole integration spike) into
several small problem/solution TSDs is preferred over one sprawling doc.

## Conventions shared by all four

1. **Open by stating the problem** (and, for integrations, the ownership boundary).
2. **A diagram only where it removes ambiguity** — not by default.
3. **Tables over prose** for anything structured.
4. **Capture the *why*** — every template ends with `Key Design Decisions` / `Open Decisions`.
5. **Every unknown is a tracked open item** with an owner — never a silent assumption. Inline
   unknowns: `[TBC — owner]`.
6. **Trace to requirements / tickets** (`DMU-030`, `REG-041`, `SFCC-123`, `ZMOBLD-263`).
7. **Link, don't embed** — reference the architecture TSD, registers, and sibling TSDs.
8. **Security by boundary, never by value** — describe where a credential lives and what it can do;
   never write a real secret.
9. **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored prose (`catalogue`, `colour`, `localisation`).

## How to use

1. Copy the chosen template to its home — a new Confluence page under
   [05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577731),
   or `.docs/` if it belongs in-repo.
2. Replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`; delete the `<!-- guidance -->` comments and any section that
   doesn't earn its place.
3. Keep the open-items table even at sign-off — a TSD with zero open items usually means something
   wasn't interrogated.

content.text:
Short answer: **no — not on its own.** The problem/solution template is the wrong *genre* for this DoD.

## Why it doesn't fit

The problem/solution template is deliberately narrow — one concrete problem, one solution (Tim's "Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"). SFCC-123's DoD is the opposite shape: **one artefact spanning four areas**, written to **brief an incoming squad**. That's a breadth the focused template is built to *exclude*.

Mapping the DoD to genres:

| DoD pillar | Best-fit template + section |
|---|---|
| Contentful integration **architecture** | **Integration** template — §1 Overview (ownership boundary: Contentful owns editorial content; SFCC owns product/price/inventory) + §2 Data Flow (Delivery / Preview / Management APIs + cache-purge webhook, SSR vs browser) |
| **Content model** requirements | *needs a dedicated "Content Model" section* (content types + fields) — this is exactly the domain-structure section the de-bloat pass trimmed |
| **Locale** setup | *needs a "Locale" section* (locale codes + Contentful bootstrap — and flag the 9-vs-11 discrepancy) |
| **SFCC-side build scope** | *needs a "Build Scope" section* + §6 Key Design Decisions + §7 Open Items |

So the right base is the **`tsd-integration-template.md`**, with three sections re-added (Content Model, Locale, Build Scope) that SFCC-123 promotes to first-class DoD requirements.

## Is this a conflict with Tim's rule?

Not really — and worth being clear about it. Tim's "one problem, not all the other stuff" is why a **briefing artefact is its own genre** (integration), separate from the focused problem/solution one. A squad briefing's single "problem" *is* "get the Contentful squad up to speed on the integration." So SFCC-123 is legitimately broad. The discipline still applies within it: keep each section lean and **link out** (to the architecture TSD, the Contentful ops page, the Product TSD §6) rather than reproducing.

## Where the problem/solution template *does* earn its place

As the format for discrete build problems the briefing references — e.g. Tim's conditional-rendering example, or a specific content-type's render logic. The briefing points to them; it doesn't inline them.

**Recommendation:** deliver SFCC-123 as **one integration-template TSD** extended with Content Model / Locale / Build Scope sections, and spin off any genuinely discrete build problems as small problem/solution TSDs linked from it.

      "value": "Overview
--------

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,
banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery
API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 3 | TEST | `test` | `npm run push:test` | zimmermann-test.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com (to be created) |
| 4 | OMS INT | `sit` | `npm run push:sit` | zimmermann-sit.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 5 | STAGE | `staging` | `npm run push:staging` | zimmermann-stg.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |
| `it` | Italian | ZimmermannEUit | en |
| `es` | Spanish | ZimmermannEUes | en |
| `en-CH` | English (EU International) | ZimmermannEUIntl | en |
| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |
| **Current types** | shoppableImage | CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage |

### Migration format

jswide4000// scripts/contentful/migrations/002-my-change.mjs
export const id = '002-my-change';
export async function up(client, { environmentId }) {
// Use the contentful-management plain client
}

Drift Detection & Promotion Rules
---------------------------------

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

bashwide4000npm run detect:drift -- --source dev --target sit
# Exits non-zero if drift found — usable as a CI gate

Scripts Reference
-----------------

| Script | Purpose | Who runs it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run setup:contentful` | Bootstrap environments, locales, API keys, and production alias | Tier 1 approver — once per space |
| `npm run config:contentful` | Populate .env with live API tokens from the space | Tier 1 approver (writes); any dev (read-only view) |
| `npm run sync:contentful` | Upsert content type definitions (dev environment only) | Any developer |
| `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target <env>` | Apply pending migrations to a target environment | CI / developer |
| `npm run detect:drift -- --source <env> --target <env>` | Diff content types between environments | CI / developer |
| `npm run promote:alias -- --target <env>` | Flip production + master aliases for a zero-downtime release | Tier 1 approver — per release |

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
106	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
107	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
108	
109	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
110	
111	| Failure | Behaviour |
112	|---|---|
113	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
114	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
115	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
116	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
117	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
118	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
119	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
120	
121	## 9. Security and privacy
122	
123	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
124	- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
125	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
126	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
127	
128	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
129	
130	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
131	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
132	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
133

# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
- Live preview in Contentful Studio
- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

# TSD Templates

Templates for authoring a **Technical Solution Document (TSD)** for the Zimmermann SFCC / PWA
programme. Derived from the existing TSD corpus in the SFCC Confluence space, refined against the
project lead's guidance.

## The one rule (per Tim)

> **A TSD addresses one problem and its solution — nothing else.**
> *"It only needs to be addressing the problem/solution. Not all the other stuff."*

Every section in every template must advance **problem → solution**. If a section doesn't, delete
it. **Link** context (architecture, requirements, sibling TSDs) rather than reproducing it. If
you're describing a *domain or system* instead of *solving a problem*, you've picked the wrong
altitude — go narrower.

## Pick the right template

| Template | Use when the problem is… | Modelled on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tsd-problem-solution-template.md`](./tsd-problem-solution-template.md) | **A single, concrete problem** — a behaviour, config, or rendering outcome. The default and most common. e.g. *"Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"*. | Tim's definition |
| [`tsd-integration-template.md`](./tsd-integration-template.md) | **Data moving correctly across systems** — a pipeline with a source of record and an integration layer. | Product · Price · Inventory · Orders · Catalogue Sync |
| [`tsd-architecture-template.md`](./tsd-architecture-template.md) | **A platform foundation** that must be fixed before feature work. Usually one per platform. | Technical Solution Design – PWA |
| [`tsd-component-template.md`](./tsd-component-template.md) | **Building a component/service/agent safely** — with component boundaries and (often) governance. | AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent |

**When in doubt, start with `tsd-problem-solution-template.md`.** Reach for one of the other three
only when the problem genuinely needs a cross-system flow map, a platform-wide foundation, or
component/governance structure. Splitting a broad brief (e.g. a whole integration spike) into
several small problem/solution TSDs is preferred over one sprawling doc.

## Conventions shared by all four

1. **Open by stating the problem** (and, for integrations, the ownership boundary).
2. **A diagram only where it removes ambiguity** — not by default.
3. **Tables over prose** for anything structured.
4. **Capture the *why*** — every template ends with `Key Design Decisions` / `Open Decisions`.
5. **Every unknown is a tracked open item** with an owner — never a silent assumption. Inline
   unknowns: `[TBC — owner]`.
6. **Trace to requirements / tickets** (`DMU-030`, `REG-041`, `SFCC-123`, `ZMOBLD-263`).
7. **Link, don't embed** — reference the architecture TSD, registers, and sibling TSDs.
8. **Security by boundary, never by value** — describe where a credential lives and what it can do;
   never write a real secret.
9. **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored prose (`catalogue`, `colour`, `localisation`).

## How to use

1. Copy the chosen template to its home — a new Confluence page under
   [05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577731),
   or `.docs/` if it belongs in-repo.
2. Replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`; delete the `<!-- guidance -->` comments and any section that
   doesn't earn its place.
3. Keep the open-items table even at sign-off — a TSD with zero open items usually means something
   wasn't interrogated.

# TSD Templates

Templates for authoring a **Technical Solution Document (TSD)** for the Zimmermann SFCC / PWA
programme. Derived from the existing TSD corpus in the SFCC Confluence space, refined against the
project lead's guidance.

## The one rule (per Tim)

> **A TSD addresses one problem and its solution — nothing else.**
> *"It only needs to be addressing the problem/solution. Not all the other stuff."*

Every section in every template must advance **problem → solution**. If a section doesn't, delete
it. **Link** context (architecture, requirements, sibling TSDs) rather than reproducing it. If
you're describing a *domain or system* instead of *solving a problem*, you've picked the wrong
altitude — go narrower.

## Pick the right template

| Template | Use when the problem is… | Modelled on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tsd-problem-solution-template.md`](./tsd-problem-solution-template.md) | **A single, concrete problem** — a behaviour, config, or rendering outcome. The default and most common. e.g. *"Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"*. | Tim's definition |
| [`tsd-integration-template.md`](./tsd-integration-template.md) | **Data moving correctly across systems** — a pipeline with a source of record and an integration layer. | Product · Price · Inventory · Orders · Catalogue Sync |
| [`tsd-architecture-template.md`](./tsd-architecture-template.md) | **A platform foundation** that must be fixed before feature work. Usually one per platform. | Technical Solution Design – PWA |
| [`tsd-component-template.md`](./tsd-component-template.md) | **Building a component/service/agent safely** — with component boundaries and (often) governance. | AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent |

**When in doubt, start with `tsd-problem-solution-template.md`.** Reach for one of the other three
only when the problem genuinely needs a cross-system flow map, a platform-wide foundation, or
component/governance structure. Splitting a broad brief (e.g. a whole integration spike) into
several small problem/solution TSDs is preferred over one sprawling doc.

## Conventions shared by all four

1. **Open by stating the problem** (and, for integrations, the ownership boundary).
2. **A diagram only where it removes ambiguity** — not by default.
3. **Tables over prose** for anything structured.
4. **Capture the *why*** — every template ends with `Key Design Decisions` / `Open Decisions`.
5. **Every unknown is a tracked open item** with an owner — never a silent assumption. Inline
   unknowns: `[TBC — owner]`.
6. **Trace to requirements / tickets** (`DMU-030`, `REG-041`, `SFCC-123`, `ZMOBLD-263`).
7. **Link, don't embed** — reference the architecture TSD, registers, and sibling TSDs.
8. **Security by boundary, never by value** — describe where a credential lives and what it can do;
   never write a real secret.
9. **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored prose (`catalogue`, `colour`, `localisation`).

## How to use

1. Copy the chosen template to its home — a new Confluence page under
   [05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577731),
   or `.docs/` if it belongs in-repo.
2. Replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`; delete the `<!-- guidance -->` comments and any section that
   doesn't earn its place.
3. Keep the open-items table even at sign-off — a TSD with zero open items usually means something
   wasn't interrogated.

Done. Here's the analysis and what it produced.

## Analysis — the key findings

**The ticket (SFCC-123).** A Squad-A spike under epic **SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments)**, reporter Jasmijn, assignee Jhoan. Objective: understand the Contentful↔SFCC integration, define the content model SFCC needs, and scope SFCC-side build **before a separate Contentful squad (own SOW) onboards**. Six explicit tasks → DoD is a single **briefing artefact** covering four pillars: integration architecture · content model · locale setup · SFCC-side build scope.

**Codebase — the SFCC side is already substantially built.** Not greenfield: `config/contentful.ts` + `contentfulMapping.ts` + `types/contentful.ts`, `hooks/useContentful.ts`, `components/contentful/{heroBanner,productHero,duplexSection,videoEmbed}` + `experiences/{shoppableImage,definitions}`, the `pages/experience` Studio route, `scripts/contentful/*` (sync, migrations, bootstrap), and CSP allowances. Plus **[.docs/integration/02-contentful.md](.docs/integration/02-contentful.md) already reads like a mini-TSD** (data flow, tokens, failure modes, open items) — so this spike is largely *document what exists + define the content model + scope the gap*, not design from scratch.

**Confluence + Jira — the content-model landscape.** The ops page (318472193) gives env topology, tokens, scripts, current types (`CollectionHero`, `ImageText`, `ShoppableImage`), and an **incomplete Human Setup Checklist** (MRT env vars, cache-purge webhook, roles, CI CMA secret = blockers). Jira shows the Sprint 1/2 content-type demand: SFCC-51 (promo banner, *Blocked*), SFCC-90 (homepage modules), SFCC-55 (footer), SFCC-82/203/190/204 (PLP editorial), SFCC-102 (PDP size-guide fallback). Sprint scope puts us in **Sprint 2 (13–24 Jul)**.

**A real blocker surfaced:** locale count is inconsistent — ops page says **9**, `02-contentful.md`/architecture TSD say **11**. That must be resolved before Contentful locale bootstrap (cloned envs inherit it).

**Template fit:** the **integration genre** is the base (cross-system flow + ownership boundary), but the DoD forces three sections the lean integration template doesn't carry by default — Content Model, Locale, Build Scope — plus a handoff-boundary section for the incoming squad. So SFCC-123 needs a *tailored* skeleton, not a generic template.

## Deliverable

New folder `specific-tsds/` under `~/Downloads/Zimmermann-PWA/TSD-Templates/`:

```
TSD-Templates/
├── README.md                       (updated — now points to specific-tsds/)
├── tsd-problem-solution-template.md   (renamed from the accidental "problemsolution")
├── tsd-integration-template.md
├── tsd-architecture-template.md
├── tsd-component-template.md
└── specific-tsds/
    ├── README.md
    └── sfcc-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md   ← the spike-specific skeleton
```

The SFCC-123 skeleton has every section **tagged to a DoD pillar / task** (`[DoD-1]`, `[Task-2]`…), is **pre-seeded** from the sources above (integration pattern, current content types + backing stories, code inventory, locale table, the blocker list) with each seed marked `[seed — verify]`, and keeps `{{placeholders}}` for what Jhoan must confirm. The locale discrepancy and the setup-checklist items are pre-loaded into its Blockers section.

Two housekeeping fixes made along the way: the `tsd-problemsolution-template.md` file was renamed to the hyphenated convention (fixing a broken README link), and the parent README now indexes the new folder.

Want me to take the skeleton one step further into a **populated draft** for Jhoan (fill the seeded sections from the sources so only the genuinely-open items remain), or leave it as the scaffold and send Jhoan the "here's a template, use it" note pointing at this file?

# TSD Template

Local mirror of the Zimmermann team's **single source of truth** for Technical Solution Documents.

- **Canonical source:** Confluence — [Technical Solution Document (TSD) Template](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/352419841). If this mirror and the Confluence page diverge, **the Confluence page wins.**
- **The template:** [`TSD-Template.md`](./TSD-Template.md)

## The rule

**One TSD = one problem.** If you're writing "and also…" in the Problem Statement, you need a second TSD.

## Structure (8 sections)

Document Information + Version History → **1.** Problem Statement → **2.** Constraints & Assumptions →
**3.** Options Analysis → **4.** Recommended Option & Rationale → **5.** Technical Implementation →
**6.** Testing & Validation → **7.** Risks & Mitigations → **8.** Decision Record (+ sign-off).

It's an options-analysis / decision-record format. A TSD is **not approved for implementation** until
Section 8 (Decision Record) is signed off by the Technical Lead.

## How to use

1. Copy `TSD-Template.md` (or the Confluence page) for each new TSD; set the Document ID to `TSD-[JIRA-KEY]`.
2. Fill each section in order; delete the ℹ️/⚠️ guidance callouts before submitting for review.
3. Keep it to one problem — split anything broader into multiple TSDs.

# TSD Templates

Templates for authoring a **Technical Solution Document (TSD)** for the Zimmermann SFCC / PWA
programme. Derived from the existing TSD corpus in the SFCC Confluence space, refined against the
project lead's guidance.

## The one rule (per Tim)

> **A TSD addresses one problem and its solution — nothing else.**
> *"It only needs to be addressing the problem/solution. Not all the other stuff."*

Every section in every template must advance **problem → solution**. If a section doesn't, delete
it. **Link** context (architecture, requirements, sibling TSDs) rather than reproducing it. If
you're describing a *domain or system* instead of *solving a problem*, you've picked the wrong
altitude — go narrower.

## Pick the right template

| Template | Use when the problem is… | Modelled on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`tsd-problem-solution-template.md`](./tsd-problem-solution-template.md) | **A single, concrete problem** — a behaviour, config, or rendering outcome. The default and most common. e.g. *"Contentful-configured SFCC IDs → conditional rendering"*. | Tim's definition |
| [`tsd-integration-template.md`](./tsd-integration-template.md) | **Data moving correctly across systems** — a pipeline with a source of record and an integration layer. | Product · Price · Inventory · Orders · Catalogue Sync |
| [`tsd-architecture-template.md`](./tsd-architecture-template.md) | **A platform foundation** that must be fixed before feature work. Usually one per platform. | Technical Solution Design – PWA |
| [`tsd-component-template.md`](./tsd-component-template.md) | **Building a component/service/agent safely** — with component boundaries and (often) governance. | AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent |

**When in doubt, start with `tsd-problem-solution-template.md`.** Reach for one of the other three
only when the problem genuinely needs a cross-system flow map, a platform-wide foundation, or
component/governance structure. Splitting a broad brief (e.g. a whole integration spike) into
several small problem/solution TSDs is preferred over one sprawling doc.

## Specific TSDs

[`specific-tsds/`](./specific-tsds/) holds **task-specific TSD skeletons** — a generic genre template
pre-shaped and seeded for one ticket, so the assignee starts from a scaffold rather than a blank page.
Current:

- [`sfcc-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md`](./specific-tsds/sfcc-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md) —
  Contentful integration briefing for [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123)
  (integration genre; sections mapped to the ticket's DoD pillars and six tasks).

## Conventions shared by all four

1. **Open by stating the problem** (and, for integrations, the ownership boundary).
2. **A diagram only where it removes ambiguity** — not by default.
3. **Tables over prose** for anything structured.
4. **Capture the *why*** — every template ends with `Key Design Decisions` / `Open Decisions`.
5. **Every unknown is a tracked open item** with an owner — never a silent assumption. Inline
   unknowns: `[TBC — owner]`.
6. **Trace to requirements / tickets** (`DMU-030`, `REG-041`, `SFCC-123`, `ZMOBLD-263`).
7. **Link, don't embed** — reference the architecture TSD, registers, and sibling TSDs.
8. **Security by boundary, never by value** — describe where a credential lives and what it can do;
   never write a real secret.
9. **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored prose (`catalogue`, `colour`, `localisation`).

## How to use

1. Copy the chosen template to its home — a new Confluence page under
   [05.1 — Architecture & Solution Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577731),
   or `.docs/` if it belongs in-repo.
2. Replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`; delete the `<!-- guidance -->` comments and any section that
   doesn't earn its place.
3. Keep the open-items table even at sign-off — a TSD with zero open items usually means something
   wasn't interrogated.

The Zimmermann team's **single source of truth** for TSDs is the Confluence page **"Technical
Solution Document (TSD) Template"** (page 352419841, SFCC space). A local mirror is kept at
`~/Downloads/Zimmermann-PWA/TSD-Templates/TSD-Template.md` — if the two diverge, Confluence wins.

**Structure (8 sections):** Document Information + Version History → 1. Problem Statement → 2.
Constraints & Assumptions → 3. Options Analysis → 4. Recommended Option & Rationale → 5. Technical
Implementation → 6. Testing & Validation → 7. Risks & Mitigations → 8. Decision Record (+ sign-off).
It's an ADR / options-driven format; a TSD is **not approved for implementation** until Section 8 is
signed off by the Technical Lead.

**Governing rule (Tim, project lead):** **one TSD = one problem** — "it only needs to be addressing
the problem/solution, not all the other stuff." Writing "and also…" in the Problem Statement means
it's a second TSD.

**Superseded:** an earlier exploratory set of 4 genre templates (problem-solution / integration /
architecture / component) plus an SFCC-123 spike skeleton were created in that folder, then
**removed 2026-07-23** once this official template was adopted. Do not recreate them. The Confluence
TSD corpus that informed that exploration is inventoried in [[project-spike-122-123-audit]].

**Why:** the official template is the team standard and is not recorded anywhere in the repo.
**How to apply:** when asked to write or review a TSD, use the official 8-section structure, hold to
"one problem per TSD", and treat the Confluence page as canonical over any local copy.
